record_body:
ACCOUNT SUMMARY
- Northbridge AI evaluating Redwood Optimize primarily for cost reduction + repeatable unit economics reporting across environments (hosted today, considering Dedicated/VPC). Very cost-sensitive; finance wants transparency, not “black box optimization.”
- Core ask: cost breakdown must be explainable at a level they can share internally (and eventually with their own enterprise customers): “show me why this request was cheaper/more expensive.”

FIRMOGRAPHICS / CONTEXT
- Product: analytics workflow platform; LLM features used for (1) long-form doc summarization for customer tickets + knowledge base, (2) doc-search + embeddings for retrieval, (3) internal support-agent assist.
- Current state: mix of LLM providers for chat + embeddings; experimenting with open models for some workloads; wants ability to compare serving configs apples-to-apples.
- Deployment direction: strong preference for VPC deployment (customer data sensitivity); Dedicated as interim step acceptable if isolation guarantees are clear.

WHAT THEY CARE ABOUT (NOTES)
- Cost sensitivity: high. They have a hard $/ticket target for support summaries and a monthly token budget cap.
  - Quote (deep dive): “We don’t need the cheapest token— we need predictable spend and a way to explain variance.”
- Latency: moderate. They can tolerate slower p95 for long summaries, but have an interactive support-agent mode that needs consistently fast responses.
- Requirements for cost model / transparency:
  - Breakdowns they requested explicitly:
    - Prefill vs decode attribution (they currently see long-context prompts as the main driver)
    - Batch efficiency impact (they plan to turn batching on for async jobs)
    - KV/prefix cache hits vs misses (they want to measure cache warming and steady state)
    - Quantization profile / model variant selection impact (they’re testing quantized configs)
    - Clear “assumptions” when signals are missing + confidence indicator
  - Must be deterministic/stable: “same inputs => same outputs” across regions/SKUs for internal reporting.
  - Must be auditable: log who accessed customer-level cost breakdown; retention controls.

RECENT ACTIVITY TIMELINE
- 2025-01-22: Inbound from their Head of AI Platform via website form. Asked specifically about Optimize and “what-if cost simulation” for batching/caching.
- 2025-01-29: Discovery call (SE: Jada). Confirmed they want VPC path; flagged SSO/SAML + audit logs as must-haves.
- 2025-02-06: Shared initial Optimize deck + high-level approach for scenario sweeps (batching on/off, cache warm/cold, quant profile swap).
- 2025-02-14: Technical deep dive on Standard Cost Model (SCM) + how Optimize consumes it. (Linked Fireflies: ff-6b2c1a)
  - Follow-up questions:
    - How do you label estimates vs metered attribution?
    - Can we export per-route breakdown to our data warehouse?
    - What happens when telemetry is delayed or missing? How do you avoid misleading outputs?
- 2025-02-21: Email recap sent w/ draft payload examples + explanation of confidence/assumptions fields. They replied asking if we can commit to versioned stability (no breaking changes) during their POC window.

TECHNICAL NOTES (FROM DEEP DIVE)
- They want Optimize to run scenario sweeps:
  - Compare batching thresholds for async summarization jobs.
  - Compare cache strategies (prefix caching for repeated instruction blocks; KV-cache hit rate targets).
  - Evaluate quant profiles for one open model family they’ve standardized on.
- They asked for an “explain endpoint” equivalent that provides contributing factors suitable for tooltips and internal dashboards.
- Data they can provide during POC:
  - prompt sets (anonymized) + distribution of input/output token lengths
  - route names + workload tags (interactive vs async)
  - current SLO targets and spend guardrails
- Integration expectation:
  - They prefer an API they can call from their own experiment runner; also want Redwood Console UI for day-to-day visibility.

SECURITY / COMPLIANCE
- Requirements captured:
  - SSO/SAML for Console
  - Audit logging: access to cost breakdown considered sensitive internally; want actor + tenant + timestamp
  - Data residency: prefer US regions only; wants explicit statement in order form
  - Retention controls: cost/usage data retention configurable (asked for 30/60/90 day options)
  - KMS: for VPC option, customer-managed keys preferred

OPEN QUESTIONS
- Which deployment do they actually start with: Dedicated vs full VPC? (They’re leaning VPC but worried about timeline.)
- Need to confirm their definition of “cost” for internal reporting:
  - technical cost attribution vs billable cost (they explicitly don’t want surprises)
  - whether they need per-request exports or aggregated rollups by route/model

NEXT STEPS (INTERNAL)
- Provide:
  - 2–3 canonical SCM example payloads matching their workloads (async summary, interactive agent, embeddings batch)
  - One-pager clarifying: estimate vs attribution, assumptions/confidence semantics, and version stability policy during POC
- Book 60-min technical follow-up (Aditya + Jada) focused on:
  - explain output fields and how they map to their unit economics dashboard
  - telemetry requirements for cache/batching/quant attribution
  - what we can support for export (CSV/API) during evaluation

RISKS
- If we can’t demonstrate explainable breakdown with confidence/assumptions, they may default to building their own measurement layer on top of provider invoices + internal runtime metrics.
- They are comparing against “simple managed endpoints” (Bedrock-style) and self-hosting; our differentiation must be transparency + controllable levers, not just raw $/token.
